data_description.components: External heat or stand-alone heat source? If your stove appears at the heater's display as its own block ("F.Wärme" by default, sometimes renamed, e.g. "Ofen"), choose External heat: the ETA control measures and charges the buffer itself, Home Assistant shows it. If it does not appear there, choose Stand-alone heat source: Home Assistant then recognises from an entity or a temperature sensor whether it heats, and it can lock the boiler.
data_description.fehlende_ausblenden: Whatever your heating system does not have gets no sensor - the pellet consumption on a log boiler, for example. Unticked, a sensor showing "-" is created instead.
data_description.verbrauch_zeitraeume: Three sensors for consumption, with a pellet price three more for the costs.
data_description.prognose: Learns from the history how much your house burns at which outside temperature and tells how long the store lasts. Up to six sensors.
data_description.wetter: Leave empty if you do not want to use a forecast. The prognosis then uses the long-term temperature average.
data_description.scan_interval: 1 to 600. The shorter, the more often the system has to answer.
data_description.schnell_intervall: Reads everything switchable, the boiler state, the room temperature and, at the fresh water module, hot water temperature, flow, buffer pump speed and circulation more often than the rest. Only applies if smaller than the polling interval.
data_description.kessel_sperre: For a stove or another device the ETA control does not know: while the switch is on, the boiler is switched off via its on/off key; afterwards Home Assistant switches it on again. In an emergency you can switch it back on at the heater's display at any time. Needs write access. Meant for your own automations or the blueprint - with the component Stand-alone heat source the switch appears by itself.

fremderzeuger.title: Stand-alone heat source
fremderzeuger.description:
For a stove or another heat source **not connected to the ETA control**: it does not appear at the heater's display, the system knows nothing about it. If your stove appears there as its own block ("F.Wärme" by default), the component External heat is the right one instead.

Here you decide how Home Assistant recognises that it is heating - with an entity, a temperature sensor or both. One of the two is required:
- **Entity only:** it heats while the entity is on.
- **Temperature sensor only:** it heats once the lock temperature is reached. The tile then gets an on/off button. Off means: the stove is ignored and locks nothing.
- **Both:** it heats when the entity is on and the lock temperature is reached.

While it heats, Home Assistant can lock the boiler and releases it afterwards. Locking needs write access - without it, the card only shows the heat source.

data.fremderzeuger_entitaet: Entity that is on while it heats

data_description.fremderzeuger_entitaet: A switch, a helper or a binary sensor. The card only shows its state.
data_description.fremderzeuger_fuehler: With a sensor, the lock temperature counts: set it in the card or with the number entity "Stand-alone heat source lock temperature" (60 °C by default). It replaces the "Lock after" waiting time.
data_description.fremderzeuger_sperrt: The boiler is switched off via its on/off key and on again afterwards - never if you had switched it off yourself. In an emergency, switch it back on at the heater's display. Without a selection nothing is locked.
data_description.fremderzeuger_sperren_nach: Without a temperature sensor: how long it must be on before the boiler is locked.
data_description.fremderzeuger_freigeben_nach: How long it must be off - or, with a sensor, 5 °C below the lock temperature - before the boiler is released.

puffer.title: Buffer tank volume
puffer.description: Your buffer tank has no total volume stored on the controller. That is the case for the 'Puffer' function block. Enter how many litres it holds - for example from the type plate or the documentation. It makes the pellet forecast more accurate. You can change the value later on the device, in the field 'Buffer tank volume'. 0 means: unknown.

raumfuehler.title: Room sensor from Home Assistant
raumfuehler.description:
These heating circuits are set up with 'Raumfühler ext. Schnittstelle' (room sensor via external interface). Pick a thermometer from Home Assistant for each circuit - the integration writes its temperature to the system every 30 seconds as the room temperature. Without a selection the system gets no room value.

The **time monitoring** is a setting of the system: if no new value arrives for that long, it discards the old one and reports 'Raumfühler: Keine Verbindung'. It is 1 minute by default - the system then reports this on every Home Assistant restart. 10 minutes bridge a restart. It is only written if you change the value.

switch_warning.title: Switching writes to your heating system
switch_warning.description:
You enabled switches. From now on Home Assistant can not only read your heating system, but also switch the boiler and the heating circuits off and on.

Please be aware:
- Switching off a heating circuit or the boiler in winter can let rooms cool down. Frost protection remains the responsibility of the heating system, not of Home Assistant.
- Anyone with access to your Home Assistant can operate these switches.
- Switches only appear where your heating system explicitly reports the variable as writable.

You can turn this off again at any time under Configure.

zeitplaene.title: Heating schedule from Home Assistant
zeitplaene.description:
Pick a **schedule helper** for each heating circuit (Settings → Devices & services → Helpers → Schedule). Each of its blocks becomes a time window of the heating system; outside the blocks the setback applies. Whenever the schedule changes, and on start-up, the integration writes the changed time windows to the system. Changes made on the display last until then.

The heating system currently has:

{programm}

Best draw the schedule exactly like this, then nothing changes when you switch it on. If it differs, the integration asks under **Settings → Repairs** before it writes anything for the first time.

The system has **at most 3 time windows per day** and works in quarter hours. A temperature is only written if a block carries one in its additional data (`temperature: 21`) - otherwise the temperatures of the heating system stay as they are. Without a selection the schedule stays untouched.

verbindungen.title: Who is connected to what
verbindungen.description: The webservices do not tell which part of the system feeds which. Pick the source for each part - this is what the lines in the **ETA Overview** card follow. The preset: the boiler charges the first buffer tank, further buffer tanks follow one after another, heating circuits and hot water hang on the last one. Buffer tanks and the transfer line both receive heat and pass it on.

abschluss.title: Almost done
abschluss.description: The heating system is set up. Finish now or add something first. Both are also available later under "Configure".

weitere_werte.title: Additional values
weitere_werte.description: Pick values from your heating system's menu tree that should appear as additional sensors. Each function block has its own field. Type part of a name there to search, for example 'Volllast' - the names are those shown on the controller. The values are only read, never written. At most {hoechstens} values.

weitere_takt.title: Polling of the additional values
weitere_takt.description: You picked {gewaehlt} values. The two sliders set how many of them the integration reads per poll and how far apart the polls are. If they do not all fit into one poll, they take turns. With the current setting each value is read every {dauer} seconds.

data_description.weitere_schnell: These values are also read by the fast polling, at the interval from the system settings. At most {schnell_hoechstens}.
data_description.weitere_je_abfrage: Fewer is easier on the heating system, but each value is read less often.
data_description.weitere_intervall: The fixed values and the fast polling run independently of this.

fehlende_werte.title: Assign missing values
fehlende_werte.description:
Not every heating system has every value, and on some systems a value sits in a different place in the menu than where the integration looks for it. In that case you can assign it here by hand.

Pick the values your controller shows and that are missing in Home Assistant. Pre-selected are values that are already assigned and values for which there is a suggestion. In the next step the integration reads the entries of the affected function blocks from the heating system, which can take a moment.

werte_zuordnen.title: Assign entries of the heating system
werte_zuordnen.description: For each value, pick the entry from your heating system's menu. Only entries from the value's function block that match in kind and unit are offered. The brackets show what the heating system currently displays - compare it with the controller. An empty field means: do not assign. The values are only read, never written.

component_not_found.title: Component "{component}" not found
component_not_found.description:
The menu of your ETA heating system contains no values for the component "{component}". Its function block is probably named differently on your controller (expected roles: {fub_names}).

Open **Settings -> Devices & Services -> ETA Web-Services -> Configure** and enter the actual name, or untick the component if your system does not have it.

raumfuehler_stumm.title: Thermometer {raumfuehler} has been silent for {stunden} hours
raumfuehler_stumm.description:
The thermometer {raumfuehler} is the room sensor of {heizkreis}, but it has not sent anything for {stunden} hours - not even the same value again. Is its battery empty?

The integration keeps writing the last value to the heating system, so the heating circuit is controlled with an old room temperature. As soon as the thermometer reports again, this notice disappears by itself. If it is gone for good, choose another one under **Settings -> Devices & services -> ETA Web-Services -> Configure**.

zeitplan_zu_voll.title: Schedule {zeitplan} does not fit on every day
zeitplan_zu_voll.description:
The heating system has at most 3 time windows per day. The schedule {zeitplan} for {heizkreis} has more blocks on these days: {tage}.

The integration does not transfer these days; the system keeps its own schedule there. Merge the blocks in the schedule and this notice disappears by itself.
